question: Who know yoga best — the devotees who, ever yoked, worship the Lord, or those who worship the imperishable, the unmanifest? (BhG 12.1–7)

sides.party: the devotees of the Lord, as the Gītā presents them
sides.position: Those who fix the mind (manas) on the Lord and worship him, ever yoked, with supreme faith, are 'the most yoked' (12.2); those who lay down all actions in him and meditate on him with undivided yoga he soon delivers from the ocean of death and saṃsāra (12.6–7).
arguments: The Lord himself holds them yuktatama, 'most yoked' (12.2).
He becomes their deliverer before long (12.7).

sides.party: the worshippers of the imperishable unmanifest, as the Gītā presents them
sides.position: Those who worship the imperishable — indefinable, unmanifest, all-pervading, unthinkable, unchanging, immovable, constant — restraining the senses, even in understanding everywhere and delighting in the welfare of all beings, also reach the Lord (12.3–4).
arguments: The text adds that their hardship is greater, since the unmanifest goal is hard for the embodied to reach (12.5).

notes: Both positions are stated within the Lord's own answer; the text does not deny that the second path reaches him. Commentators construe the passage differently: Śaṅkara takes the imperishable as brahman beyond attributes and its worshippers as the knowers the Gītā elsewhere calls the Lord's very self (7.18), so that 12.2's praise concerns those not yet fit for that path; Rāmānuja takes the imperishable here as the individual self's own nature, and devotion to the Lord as the quicker and easier way. These readings belong to the commentaries, not to the verses (to be verified against the bhāṣyas).
